question: Does prefix-rtc beat the public model at continuous coverage 400 over 30 seeds; do a 5 Euler-step graph and a delay 0-8 / 8000-update retrain keep synchronous success and improve continuous execution?

protocol.scene: mug, one trial per seed and condition, unchanged 2 ms physical scoring, base-drift limit, 120 s timeout
protocol.browser: Chrome (playwright-core, headless, Metal WebGPU); every run first passed the page parity check 3/3

snapshots.exp-tree (port 5191): commit 82a5e2c, empty diff: all prefix-rtc and public runs

exp-tree3 (port 5193).overlay: e01ffd6 versions of src/learning/learned-onnx-contract.ts, src/learning/learned-model-download.ts, tests/learned-model-download.test.ts, tests/learned-onnx-contract.test.ts, tests/learned-worker.test.ts, tests/static-site-assembly.test.ts (registry only; reproduce with git show e01ffd6:<file> over a checkout of 82a5e2c)

protocol.gates: pre-registered: a new graph proceeds to continuous trials only with synchronous seeds 3000-3009 >= 9/10; v2 coverage 600 extends to 3029 only with >= 5/10 on 3000-3009
protocol.voidedRuns: records ending with status running and error "RTC queue underflow" (the executor stops when an inference returns after its queue ran out) are kept, counted as failures in the primary test and reported excluded as a sensitivity check; nothing was rerun

task4.voidedDriverMismatch: a first pass on a snapshot of e01ffd6 (includes the 9a5a081 menu split) never started: the trial driver could not find the direct single-task controls, which moved to &direct=1; 20 runs, no physics, kept in work/followups-2026-10-26/voided-driver-mismatch

skipped.prefixRtcV2E5Continuous400: synchronous gate 8/10 < 9/10 (the graph stays registered and is marked unevaluated)

rawData: work/prefix-rtc-2026-10-26/runs and work/followups-2026-10-26/runs (outside Git; record.json, screenshots, driver logs)

forceLimitedSuccess.definition: successes whose run peakUnintendedForce (force audit, all 2 ms steps) is <= 100 N, the original unintended-force limit of the teacher-quality gate; the task scorer itself does not apply it; synchronous runs record no audit

contacts.definition: collisionEpisodes = task scorer episodes with robot contact force > 25 N (hysteresis 15 N), excluding floor contacts and finger contacts with an object while closing (<0.5) or held; auditedUnintendedPairs = force-audit pairs (synchronous runs record no audit)

currentBuildSmoke.build: 16aa6a8 working tree on the dev server (current menu UI), ?mode=learned&direct=1&executor=async&model=<id>&gripPause=0&rtcCoverage=400, mug seed 3000, one run each
currentBuildSmoke.note: Smoke check only (one run each, not a rate). The current UI has no 検証結果を保存 button, so no record.json was saved; results are from the page status in the driver logs and the final screenshot. The page also showed that the planner model could not be prepared in this headless profile (not used by &direct=1).

conclusion.task1: prefix-rtc beats the public model at continuous coverage 400 over 30 seeds (16/30 vs 4/30, one-sided Fisher p=0.0011; 0.0004 with the 4 underflow-voided runs excluded). Seeds 3010-3029 are harder for every executor: synchronous public 15/20, prefix-rtc 15/20. Task 1 ran under noisier timing (all 4 underflows, a few slow playbacks) than the later candidate runs, which were not interleaved with their comparators.
conclusion.task2: prefix-rtc-e5 (same weights, 5 Euler steps): inference ~0.60-0.63 s instead of ~0.89 s, playback ~0.69x instead of ~0.47x, synchronous 9/10, continuous 400 21/30 (vs public p=8e-6; vs prefix-rtc 16/30 p=0.14, 0.28 with voided runs excluded).
conclusion.task3: prefix-rtc-v2 (delays 0-8, 8000 updates): offline prefix error ~15% lower at every delay, synchronous 10/10, continuous 400 23/30 (vs public p=7e-7; vs prefix-rtc p=0.052, 0.13 with voided runs excluded), coverage 600 4/10. Its 5-step graph failed the synchronous gate (8/10).
conclusion.forces: Counting only successes whose run peak unintended force stays <= 100 N (the original teacher-quality limit, not part of task scoring): e5 15/30, v2 13/30, prefix-rtc 12/30, public 4/30 (vs public p=0.0024 / 0.010 / 0.020). v2 has the most successes above 100 N (10 of 23, including seed 3024 at 5391 N run peak with one 3073 N finger-mug contact). The ranking v2 > e5 holds only for raw success, not for force-limited success.
conclusion.contacts: Continuous execution raises the count of >25 N robot contact episodes for all prefix models (success-run medians 14-24 vs 1-2 synchronous on the same seeds); v2 is high even synchronously (27). The audited unintended pairs are almost all finger-mug (open-hand finger touching the mug), not table or basket; the public model shows the same pairs.
conclusion.notAdopted: Nothing changes on the public site or the default executor; candidates stay local and hash-pinned. Choosing a candidate for the site or the video is the user's decision.
